column2: Full fine-tuning (structure_module + diffusion_conditioning): tune learning rate, warmup and decay schedule (cosine or linear), steps and weight decay. Start from configs/finetune_diffusion.yaml.

LoRA: rank, alpha, which linear layers to adapt (attention only, transitions only, conditioning too), learning rate, and a possible alpha/rank rescaling. Start from configs/finetune_diffusion_lora.yaml.
Weight averaging: EMA of the trained weights (decay 0.99 to 0.999) and/or averaging checkpoints of one run, exported and scored instead of the last step.

Which parameters to train: last N score_model blocks only, atom encoder/decoder only, token transformer only, diffusion_conditioning only, or adding the confidence/trunk modules. Compare equal-compute runs.

The training objective: diffusion_loss_weight vs distogram weight, smooth-lDDT and ligand_loss_weight/nucleotide weights (diffusion_loss_args), per-atom weighting toward the ligand and pocket, and diffusion_multiplicity / sampling_steps in training.

How crystals are presented: crop size and pocket-conditioning probability, binder-pocket sampling, oversampling high-resolution or ligand-rich entries, filtering low-quality entries, random rotations/augmentation, MSA use. No val/test or non-hit data in the diffusion loss.

Staying close to the pretrained model: L2-SP / weight-decay toward the pretrained weights, layer-wise learning rates, weight interpolation between pretrained and fine-tuned weights (WiSE-FT style), early stopping chosen on validation.
Training length and batch: more steps (3000+), gradient accumulation, learning-rate warmup length, multiplicity, and how validation RMSD changes along the run (score several checkpoints of one run).

Variance and ensembling: repeat the best known recipe (check the leaderboard and messages) with several training seeds, weight-average runs, and measure which differences on the board are real. Also report the training-seed spread.

Training is cheap relative to sampling: keep weights close to stock but test whether fine-tuning helps at inference settings that stay within the frozen predict config only for scoring (do not edit the frozen files); explore combining the best weights of the other agents (merge or average their exported checkpoints from agents/*/results/runs/*/boltz_ckpt) and report whether the merge beats each parent.
